title: Follow up qa-v1-theory-4d4155a911aa169be0be4ac1
behavioral_concerns: follow up: ApprovedQAChecks fingerprint includes WorkingDirectory (absolute target), causing CheckCatalogFingerprint to be target-path dependent and destabilizing QAMap semantic identity

evidence.summary: ApprovedQAChecks sets WorkingDirectory to absolute target and hashes it via fingerprintQAValue
QAMap builds CheckCatalogFingerprint as fingerprintQAValue(checks) where checks contain absolute WorkingDirectory descriptors
QATargetIdentity and QAApprovedCheckRef definitions show CheckCatalogFingerprint is persisted and validated but excluded from QASemanticIdentity
Existing test verifies determinism only within same target (README.md vs internal/a.go ordering) not across different absolute targets

theories.claim: ApprovedQAChecks fingerprint includes absolute WorkingDirectory, making CheckCatalogFingerprint target-path dependent and destabilizing QAMap content identity
theories.basis: internal/sprint/qa_prompt.go:75 constructs QACheckDescriptor with WorkingDirectory=filepath.Clean(target) (absolute manifest.Target); 79-86 copies descriptor with Fingerprint="" and hashes via fingerprintQAValue which serializes all remaining fields including WorkingDirectory. internal/sprint/qa_map.go:106 calls ApprovedQAChecks(manifest.Target, ...) and 114-115 does CheckCatalogFingerprint=fingerprintQAValue(checks) over slice containing those descriptors, therefore catalog hash embeds absolute path. QAMap stores it at internal/sprint/qa_types.go:328 and validates at 682 but QASemanticIdentity at 478-484 deliberately excludes CheckCatalogFingerprint from attempt/map ID, so map ID stable but serialized QAMap bytes/artifact digests diverge per checkout path, violating reproducible/portable fingerprint expectations.
theories.verification_surface: Static read-only inspection of ApprovedQAChecks -> fingerprintQAValue -> QAMap.CheckCatalogFingerprint propagation; compare descriptor JSON hashed for two different absolute targets with same logical goPaths/budgets
theories.confirmation_condition: Fingerprint of descriptor for same args/budgets differs when computed with target=/tmp/a vs /tmp/b, or CheckCatalogFingerprint varies solely by absolute target path
theories.refutation_condition: Fingerprint computation normalizes or excludes WorkingDirectory (e.g., strips/redacts WorkingDirectory before canonicalQAJSON) so same logical check yields identical digest across absolute targets
theories.inconclusive_condition: Fingerprint path inclusion cannot be determined from assigned context paths without additional code outside shard
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Read-only file search for ApprovedQAChecks, WorkingDirectory, fingerprintQAValue, CheckCatalogFingerprint; no writes, process execution, or filesystem mutation

theories.outcome_reason: Code inspection confirms WorkingDirectory (absolute target) is retained in the value passed to fingerprintQAValue and thus incorporated into QACheckDescriptor.Fingerprint and downstream QAMap.CheckCatalogFingerprint. No redaction or relative-path normalization occurs before hashing, so catalog fingerprint is host absolute-path dependent, causing QAMap normalized bytes and digests to differ per clone location, contrary to contract-configuration persistence expectations for deterministic semantic identity.
